purpose: test whether directional Adam-preconditioned utility improves on raw gradient magnitude and the frozen activation rule without expensive second-order credit

rule.score: per-token cosine between sampled FFN-weight gradient contributions and reconstructed realized Adam update direction, aggregated by layer and token type with EMA beta 0.2
rule.parameter_samples: 128 fixed uniformly sampled entries per FFN weight matrix, 256 per layer
rule.timing: strictly one-step lagged after the real optimizer step; first step exact-budget random; unseen types use observed layer mean
rule.scope: FFN weights only; no biases, attention, weight decay, Hessian, current-batch gradients, or full per-token parameter gradients

verification: full-parameter special case matched direct factorized gradient/Adam cosine with zero numerical error in the CPU self-test; MPS smoke passed
primary_endpoints: adam_alignment minus raw gradient-high sparse loss at every evaluation
adam_alignment minus low_max_abs sparse loss at every evaluation
adam_alignment minus random and shuffled low_max_abs sparse loss
dense-fewer comparison at matched total cost including auxiliary operations
dense evaluation, realized activity, token-type coverage, and sampled alignment statistics

decision_rules.advance: adam_alignment must beat gradient-high and low_max_abs at step 200 in all four regimes
decision_rules.stop: if it only lands between raw gradients and low_max_abs, stop directional-gradient development
decision_rules.fresh_confirmation: only a rule satisfying advance earns unchanged replication on bodies 9 and 10
decision_rules.development_level_3_signal: the qualifying rule must also beat dense-fewer at matched total cost in all four regimes

prohibited: increasing the parameter sample or changing beta after seeing results
claiming an exact full-gradient or Hessian method
using current-step gradients or an additional forward pass
claiming practical efficiency from wins over random or raw gradients alone
